articleTitle: Assessing Performance of Building Environment Simulator using MAS Technology in Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A built-in thermal environment simulator with multi agent simulation technique was proposed in the study. The simulator works on only datasets obtained from BEMS and completes its simulation in a short time without solving complex governing equations. The simulator was implemented and applied to an actual building for a year. The accuracy of the simulation was confirmed on one year field data.

articleTitle: CFD Simulation for Gas Detection in Disaster Areas Using Multiple Micro-Drones
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper describes our gas detection system in disaster areas using multiple micro-drones. Our goal is to create a system in which multiple drones have different functions and work together to assess the situation in disaster areas. The system will determine the state of the environment, including temperature, humidity, air velocity, and gas concentration, as detected by the drone. The system then uses Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) to identify the location of gas leaks and predict the effects of future gas dispersion. Early detection of gas leaks, one of the causes of secondary disasters, is extremely important from the perspective of disaster prevention. In this paper, we attempt to investigate gas detection methods in disaster areas using multiple drones, both experimentally and by simulation.

articleTitle: Image Similarity between Masked and Unmasked Face for Consumer Electronics Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Face recognition has become essential as a convenient biometric-based solution for a plethora of different consumer electronics applications, including access control systems, intelligent environments, smartphone authentication systems and so on. Early in 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic caused the widespread use of face masks, which become essential for containing the outbreak. The masks cause a visible alteration in facial appearance, covering almost the 50% of the human face. In this work, an image similarity technique is applied to assess the difference between two images of the same face wearing or not wearing a face mask. Cosine Similarity measure-based Algorithm (CSA) was used to objectively infer the difficulties that modern facial recognition algorithms, based on deep learning techniques, encounter when dealing with a masked face.

articleTitle: Evaluation System for Martial Arts Demonstration from Smartphone Sensor Data Using Deep Neural Networks on Noisy Labels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Smartphones and smartwatches are widespread. Devices have with sensors. Research activities to obtain data from sensors to recognize sports motion and find modifications are on the rise. These studies make it possible to provide movement feedback without a coach. However, a few studies have focused on the correctness of the movement, or which parts of the movement are correct. Herein, we propose a method to evaluate the movements of a martial arts demonstration based on sensor data obtained from a smartphone. In the demonstration, several movements, such as punching and kicking, are performed. The coach considers each movement and evaluates the overall movement comprehensively. Regarding the coach evaluation, we evaluate sensor data by dividing the data and using machine learning. This method was applied to the acceleration data of taekwondo demonstrations. It was shown to reproduce the instructor's score with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Efficient Digital Television System Booting Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents Booting procedure and insight of Digital Television System. Compared to computer, Digital Television System requires low-power mode in WAIT-state and normal-power mode in NORMAL rich operation. We show our system can reduce the number of storage devices used for booting and decrease the booting time. We can also save cost and power consumption for products.

articleTitle: Cyclist Speed Estimation Using Accelerometer, Gyroscope, and Monocular Camera
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: V2X communication and its supporting systems are significant for the future of fully autonomous driving systems because onboard sensing may suffer from its limited detection range or physical obstruction. Cyclists are more dynamic compared to pedestrians, and their lack of signals to show their intentions of crossing and turning to autonomous vehicles may lead to traffic accidents. This paper proposes to estimate cyclists' speed using data from portable devices such as smartphones to support V2X communication systems for autonomous driving. Prior research shows that the data gathered from a smartphone's accelerometer and gyroscope allow the model to estimate a cyclist's speed that surpasses the GPS-based speed estimation method. However, the results of the accelerometer and gyroscope-based method were noisy. On the other hand, visual sensors have been widely used for visual odometry. Monocular visual odometry may encounter issues caused by scale drift and dynamic objects. This paper aims to integrate three sensors, an accelerometer, a gyroscope, and a monocular camera, into a Machine Learning model to improve the performance of cyclist speed estimation. A series of experiments have been conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Deep Knowledge Distillation Learning for Efficient Wearable Data Mining on the Edge
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Wearable data mining on the edge is essential for consumer electronics and providing real-time insights to the users. However, the challenge lies in the high computing complexity and energy consumption of the algorithms, especially the advanced deep neural networks. Focusing on this challenge, we in this research have proposed a deep knowledge distillation learning algorithm to achieve a light-weight edge-deployable deep learning model. We take a special interest in the Electrocardiogram-based cardiac disease detection application. More specifically, we have firstly designed a heavy teacher model for cardiac disease detection. We then have leveraged the soft target distribution of the teacher model to supervise the training of a lightweight student model. In such a way, the student model can learn the knowledge from the teacher model, with an energy-efficient structure that has significantly less parameters. Evaluated on the cardiac disease detection task, our framework has demonstrated promising effectiveness, and this study will therefore greatly advance efficient wearable data mining on the edge in consumer electronics.

articleTitle: Speaker Verification Systems with Robustness to Various Noises Using Sparse Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, speaker verification systems have been used in various places. Among them, we focused on a speaker verification system with robustness to various noises. Currently, speaker verification is achieved using Deep Neural Networks (DNN), but the accuracy is greatly degraded with background noise and conversational voice. Therefore, we propose SparseSincNet, which applies sparse processing to SincNet, a highly accurate speaker verification model, and build a speaker verification system that can be used in various noisy environments. As a result, the accuracy of the proposed method is 13.8% higher than that of SincNet when white noise with a signal-to-noise ratio of 20 dB is used. Moreover, the Sparse algorithm has the potential for faster inference speeds, which could lead to smaller authentication systems.

articleTitle: Vehicle CAN Bus Data Prediction Using Transformers with Auxiliary Decoder Loss
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A controller area network (CAN) bus carries control signals in manually and autonomously driven vehicles. A temporal analysis of CAN data provides insight into control decisions translated to motion. The motion of a vehicle is planned on the perception of surroundings using inputs of optical sensors with spatial data. The translation of the spatial information in temporal analysis is learned in deep learning techniques that primarily rely on the temporal data for loss computation which is considered insufficient for a fair translation. This work presents a novel loss function that adds prediction of spatial features decoding to the loss of temporal prediction of CAN bus data. A deep network is proposed which uses a transformer encoder to encode images and CAN data and a convolution decoder that generates the spatial features. The experimentation with the nuScenes data set shows promising results with the proposed idea in CAN bus data prediction. Code is available online to use the proposed loss function in more applications. https://github.com/Aasimrafique/AuxililaryVisualLoss.

articleTitle: Circuit Design of Memristor-based GRU and its Applications in SOC Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Gated recurrent unit (GRU) is a variant of recurrent neural network (RNN), which is widely used in applications and tasks related to sequence data processing. However, traditional GRU networks based on von Neumann computing construction, have been facing challenges such as big data dimension and high real-time requirements. Meanwhile, limited internal storage resources and external storage bandwidth have jointly limited the overall performance of hardware implementation of GRU networks. Based on these, a compact scheme for the hardware circuit design of memristor-based GRU network is presented, along with the concrete circuit design of nonlinear activation and the linear matrix operation. The entire scheme is validated by the application of the Lithium ion battery state of charge (SOC) estimation. This work is expected to integrate the neuromorphic electronics and battery management systems, and further promote the development of electric vehicles in smart cities.

articleTitle: Implementation of Continuous Dyeing Process Scheduling Algorithm based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The dyeing process is a process that reproduces the color of the fabric desired by the buyer and realizes the feeling of touch. In particular, the dyeing process is a parallel process in which there are many dyeing machines with different capacities. Further, the dyeing process is affected by the dyeing color and concentration in the previous process. We propose a continuous dyeing process that can improve productivity and dyeing quality. The proposed algorithm is based on genetic algorithms and deals with both the whole process and the staining process. The dyeing process is an optimization problem that divides and allocates the order quantity according to the capacity of multiple dyeing machines. The genetic algorithm is suitable as an algorithm for finding an optimized solution for this problem. The proposed algorithm simplifies and divides the order quantity by integer programming, and constructs chromosomes. It then runs a genetic algorithm and allocates the dyeing machines so that the continuous dyeing process can be performed while minimizing delivery dates and machine cleaning, which are the objective functions. The proposed algorithm was able to confirm a five hours saving effect based on the existing three days production situation data.

articleTitle: Prediction-Reconstruction VLSI architecture with efficient pipelining for VVC Decoder
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Versatile Video Coding (VVC) introduced newly proposed tools to improve the compression rate of ultra-high definition video. However, this increases both the complexity of decoder implementation and the cost when implementing with System on Chip (SOC). HEVC decoder could perform hardware pipelining in smaller unit than the CTU size using the symmetric CU split method. However, VVC includes an asymmetric CU split method, increasing not only complexity but also pipeline memory size. This paper presents an architecture that designs a pipeline between internal processing blocks to satisfy video decoder performance and reduce hardware costs. In particular, it proposes a method of minimizing the memory cost used in Intra / Inter Prediction and Reconstruction Path, and by implementing Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI), the result is derived using the VVC compression stream of 4K resolution.

articleTitle: Automotive Multi-Chip System with Cache Coherent Interconnect for Pipelined Parallel Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Due to the ever increasing computing performance required by Autonomous Driving (AD), the AD systems of high-end vehicles are equipped with multiple automotive SoCs. For chip-to-chip interconnect interface, cache coherent interconnect interface can be a good candidate since it supports shared-memory system by providing a single globally shared address space. With shared-memory system, the entire system can be managed by a single OS or hypervisor. Applications also do not need explicit data transfer and synchronization through I/O devices to communicate across the chip. However, since the interconnect between chips takes much higher latency compared to on-chip interconnect, significant performance degradation can occur when a host chip accesses memory in a remote chip. This is a painful problem of cache coherent Non-Uniform Memory Access (cc-NUMA) systems. This paper proposes an effective cache coherent interconnect architecture and automotive application binding scheme for automotive cc-NUMA system. The experimental results show that the system performance is improved by 22 % on average with the proposed architecture.

articleTitle: Visual inspection system using multi-layer feature sparse coding with acoustic support
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Visual inspections are conducted in manufacturing industries to determine whether all or a certain number of products are non-defective or defective by visually inspecting them before shipment. However, improvements and revisions are required owing to the long hours of simple work and mental strain involved. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based anomaly detection, which determines whether a product is non-defective or defective, is attracting attention as an alternative to human visual inspection for reducing human workload. AI-based anomaly detection provides the inspector with a heat map to visualize the defective area and condition. In this study, we developed a method to improve the judgment of defective products that slip through AI-based anomaly inspection by providing a heat map image as an auditory stimulus. We investigated the effectiveness of a hybrid inspection method combining AI-based anomaly inspection using visual information and anomaly inspection using sound by converting visual information (a heat map) into auditory information. The visual abnormality inspection AI was able to achieve a detection accuracy of over 80% by changing the image. The overall correct response rate for anomaly inspection using sound was 83.3%.

articleTitle: Adaptive Noise Canceller Algorithm with an SNR-Based Stepsize and Controlled Averaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a noise canceller adaptation algorithm with an SNR-based stepsize and controlled averaging. A first and a second SNR with different averaging constants are used one after the other to control the stepsize in adaptation. The averaging constants reflect the accuracy of the SNR estimate such that lower accuracy is offset with a larger averaging constant. The first SNR estimate with lower accuracy guarantees the initial coefficient growth whereas the second SNR estimate provides more accurate adaptation control. Changeover from the first to the second SNR estimate takes place when the coefficient growth is saturated. Evaluations with clean speech and noise recorded at a busy station demonstrate that the coefficient error by the proposed algorithm is as much as 6dB smaller than that by conventional algorithms with a constant averaging.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Discretization Effect Towards Numerical Data for Data Protection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We evaluated a method to protect individual privacy. Existing privacy methods create a trade-off between confidentiality and openness. To balance these, we evaluated the effect of discretization on protecting confidential numerical data. We evaluated a method that uses discretization by frequency or binning and adjusted the discretization parameter. By adjusting the number of bins, we showed that anonymized data is 30% harder to de-anonymize during data reconstruction attacks.

articleTitle: Direct Decoding Adopting LDM in Partial Reception Band in Next-Generation DTTB
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recently, research is being conducted for ultrahigh-definition television(UHDTV) broadcasting in Japan. Advanced digital terrestrial television broadcasting(DTTB) will enable 4K·8K broadcasting. One of transmission schemes studied in advanced DTTB is layered division multiplexing-band segmented transmission-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing(LDM-BST-OFDM). LDM-BST-OFDM is implemented in ATSC3.0. On LDM-BST-OFDM transmission scheme, direct decoding and sequential decoding are proposed as decoding schemes. Gray mapped LDM(GLDM) is expected to improve reception characteristic of the lower layer(LL) in direct decoding. In this paper, required carrier-to-noise ratio(CNR) in direct decoding is evaluated. Firstly, the effectiveness of GLDM is indicated in required CNR of the LL. Secondly, subcarrier modulation of fixed reception is changed from U-16QAM to U-4096QAM. And fixed reception characteristics with U-16QAM is best among them. Thirdly, direct decoding against the required CNR of fixed recention is evaluated.

articleTitle: Color Interpolation with Full Resolution for Hybrid RGB-IR CMOS Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, many applications using paired RGB and Near-infrared (NIR) images have been proposed in camera vision and image signal processors. With the current progress of the CMOS image sensor technology, manufacturing a CMOS image sensor with a unique spectrum filter array is becoming mature. Different spectrum filter pixels integrate into the same chip produced in the industry, which supports the one-shot acquisition of each spectrum image signal. RGB and NIR-integrated CMOS Image Sensor is an example of this paper's discussion called RGB-IR Hybrid sensor. Regarding the RGB-IR filter array, two CFA types have been produced in the industry. The kind of CFA which is the paper discussion that half of the Red/Blue pixels are replaced with the NIR pixels but keep the G pixel the same. However, such CFAs have less color information to generate the RGB image. This paper presents a convenient interpolation use in the RGB-IR class of panchromatic arrays to improve the image quality like false color edge, zipper effect on edge, and noise besides compatibility with Bayer CFA of total RGB pixels sensor solution.

articleTitle: Total-Ionizing-Dose Tolerance Analysis of a Radiation-Hardened Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Space systems and robots used at nuclear power plants require radiation-hardened image sensors that can function for long periods in an environment with intense radiation. This paper presents a radiation-hardened image sensor from which the on-chip control circuit has been removed. The image sensor can therefore be controlled entirely from outside of the environment. This paper clarifies the total-ionizing-dose tolerance of the radiation-hardened image sensor.

articleTitle: Color Reproduction of Multi-Pigment Color Electronic Papers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The next generation of multi-pigment color electronic paper (ePaper) has been proposed, but the design issues of its color reproduction pipeline are not well-addressed yet. A new approach, which combines Sigmoidal Gaussian Cusp Knee (SGCK) and Multiple Anchor Points approaches, to color reproduction of color ePaper has been proposed in this paper. The experimental results show that the contrast, color saturation, and color correctness for the images shown on the color ePaper have been significantly improved.

articleTitle: iMirror: An Intelligent Gait Recognition Mirror for Rehabilitation of Patients with Parkinson's Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel mirror-based gait recognition system, designated as iMirror, which adopts an AI edge module and walking images capturing by an imaging camera to perform skeleton and gait recognition functionalities. The experimental results show that iMirror can effectively identify the human step length and step shaking angle when walking on the parallel bar. As a result, iMirror is suitable for replacing the traditional mirror in front of the original rehabilitation parallel bar as a tool for analyzing the gait performance of Parkinson's patients.

articleTitle: Stage-Stopped Belief Propagation Decoding for Polar Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Capacity-achieving polar codes have grown attention in recent years, and the belief propagation (BP) algorithm is one way to decode them. With the help of min-sum approximation and G-matrix early termination schemes, it has been proven that complexity and computation can be further reduced without significant performance loss. Although G-matrix early termination is a strong stopping criterion, there are still some redundant cycles that need to be reduced, since G-matrix early termination only reduces the computation caused by redundant iterations but not the redundant cycles inside of one iteration. In this paper, a stage-stopping BP algorithm with round-trip scheduling is proposed to reduce the redundant computation. Different thresholds for different signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regions are simulated to seek the proper combination.

articleTitle: Multi-Layer Attention-based State Representation for the Reinforcement Learning of Visual Servoing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose multi-layer attention-based state representation for robotic visual servoing using reinforcement learning. It is challenging for a robot to manipulate an object that it has never been trained on, which can occur in real use cases. Multiple attention layers allow the model to extract the spatial features of the object in the scene from high to low resolution in latent space. Using the extracted features allows the robotic controller model to learn more robust trajectory planning. We evaluated and compared the robustness of our method with that of other methods on a fetch-reach task in a simulation by randomly scaling the size of the target object. The results demonstrated that our method yielded the highest success rate, with the most efficient trajectory planning, which indicates that our state representation model provided more useful information that enabled visual servoing to perform more robustly for unseen objects.

articleTitle: HMD in General Public for Training: Case Study of Standardized Dementia-Friendly Initiative in Japan
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Use of Head-Mounted Display (HMD) and Virtual Reality has become popular and the consumer market is growing rapidly with some help from the trend of metaverse. However, practical use of HMD is still limited to either personal use for entertainment, experimental use within industrial training or professional training, or for research purpose within academic practice. Therefore, this paper introduced the HMD to a practical training program, a standardized dementia friendly initiative which trains the general public to become a “Dementia Supporters” in Japan. The training program was performed by a formal lecturer for “Dementia Supporters”, and supporting staffs who are not familiar with VR technology. The HMD was used to show a short movie of a first-person view in 360 degree, associated with a normal dramatic movie about a story of dementia. Of the 157 participants who applied to participate the training program, 62 participants in the intervention group experienced the HMD, were evaluated using the User Experience Questionnaire and the Simulator Sickness Questionnaire. The evaluation results clarified that the training program using HMDs has positive effect in the index of appearance and practicality, low evaluation in the novelty, and there were no sickness observed within the participants. These results may imply the use of HMD to the general public is practical with carefully designed VR contents and training program.

articleTitle: Lightweight Text Spotting for Interactive User Experience in Mixed Reality
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We propose a machine learning-aided semantic understanding framework of surrounding scenes for intelligent human-computer interaction in mixed reality (MR). The proposed framework perceives semantic information from the front-view camera of MR glasses with fast and accurate machine learning-based scene text spotting models. Furthermore, it allows MR glasses to generate corresponding virtual objects automatically to coincide with the surrounding scenes without further user intervention. Moreover, for near real-time computing capability, scene text spotting models serve as a remote service under the client-server model in the framework to break through the computing bottleneck of wearable devices. We demonstrate the framework with Microsoft HoloLens 2, and experiment results show its feasibility in improving user experience under self-collected real-world scenarios. In addition, the proposed client-server architecture provides 0.77 seconds of computational time per frame on average, which is not only on average 11.8 times faster than the client-only architecture but also achieves near real-time computation. To investigate the usability of text spotting algorithms in real-world applications, we also compare several state-of-the-art scene text spotting approaches regarding recognition precision and computational time.

articleTitle: Removing Host Interventions from GPU Accelerated Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel scheme removing host interventions from OpenCL execution in GPU-accelerated neural network. Our scheme must satisfy two folds; i) remove host interventions between CPU and GPU interactions, ii) use previous OpenCL kernels without modification. To do so, we propose a Delegator-based OpenCL execution method providing a good solution in such situation. Experimental result shows that our scheme reduces execution latency into 0.43.

articleTitle: Investigating Suitability of Inverse Tone Mapping for Medical Images
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Standard dynamic range (SDR) technology has been the foundation of medical imaging to this day, making medical images lack contrast and details. To address this issue, a feasible option before adopting high dynamic range (HDR) technology in the medical image capturing is to use inverse tone mapping (iTMO) to convert SDR images into HDR images. This approach can synthetically recover some of the information lost during the SDR capturing process and increase the contrast and overall brightness of the image. This paper is the first study that evaluates the performance of existing famous iTMOs for the medical images. In our study we used Breast Cancer Biopsy whole slide images as an example type of medical images. Our performance evaluations showed that some iTMOs achieved a significant improvement in visual quality, offering a better contrast and details, and the potential to help the accuracy at diagnosis phases.

articleTitle: Disentanglement-Based Multi-Vehicle Detection and Tracking for Gate-Free Parking Lot Management
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Multiple object tracking (MOT) techniques can help to build gate-free parking lot management systems purely under vision-based surveillance. However, conventional MOT methods tend to suffer long-term occlusion and cause ID switch problems, making applying them directly in crowded and complex parking lot scenes challenging. Hence, we present a novel disentanglement-based architecture for multi-object detection and tracking to relieve the ID switch issues. First, a background image is disentangled from the original input frame; then, MOT is applied separately to the background and original frames. Next, we design a fusion strategy that can solve the ID switch problem by keeping track of the occluded vehicles while considering complex interactions among vehicles. In addition, we provide a dataset with annotations in severe occlusions parking lot scenes that suits the application. The experiment results show our superiority over the state-of-the-art trackers quantitatively and qualitatively.

articleTitle: Research on the Effect of Flickering Speed on the Utility of Warning Incandescent Light
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a stimulation rhythm suitable for a longer duration of continuous flashing of white light, which gives enough push and less oppression. Experimental test results show that BPM 120 has a high reminder and a lesser sense of pression. At the same time, the average value of Neurosky MindWave eSense Meditation of BPM 120 is the highest one above BPM 110, and the standard deviation is obviously the smallest one above BPM 90, with the smallest degree of dispersion. Therefore, BPM 120 may be a tempo that keeps flashing white light for a long time, giving people a sufficient sense of prompting, and at the same time feeling less oppressive.

articleTitle: Single Image Fence Removal Using Fast Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Fences extensively cover the image in a variety of shapes, making fence removal from the image is a challenging task. Most fence removal in a single image is performed in two stages: fence area estimation and inpainting as shown in the Fig 1. Conventional fence detection has utilized information such as edge information, luminance information, and fence regularity to deal with various shapes. However, those methods have resulted in missing fences and false detections of structures similar to fences. In this paper, we propose a network that incorporates a module that includes a fast Fourier transform. This allows us to extract global features of fences that extensively cover the image in various shapes. Furthermore, we create a dataset of rectangular fences, which is not available in previous datasets. Experimental results on existing and proposed datasets show that our method achieves better results, both quantitatively and qualitatively, by suppressing missing fences and false positives of other structures.

articleTitle: Architecture Design of AVS3 Fractional Motion Estimation for 4K UHD Video Coding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The third generation of video coding standards (AVS3) has significantly improved video coding performance. It adopts three block division mechanisms, including Binary-Tree (BT) division, Quad-Tree (QT) division and extended Quad-Tree (EQT) division. These three block division increase the computation amount of fractional pixel motion estimation (FME), making it difficult to implement a real-time FME hardware. This paper proposes a 17-point fractional pixel parallel search algorithm and small-sized motion vector substitution(MVS) algorithm to reduce the number of CUs for FME. Combined with these two hardware friendly algorithms, we design a parallel pipeline architecture suitable for CUs with sizes from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$64\times 64$</tex>. FME hardware module is divided into four circuits to process CUs of different sizes. Each circuit is divided into eight flow modules to ensure that the clock cycles required by each circuit are almost the same. These eight flow modules include data preparation, interpolation, search, rate-distortion optimization (RDO) and other modules to calculate fractional pixel motion vector (FMV) of CUs. MVS module uses the deduced FMVs to substitute FMV of the remaining CUs. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithms have 0.28% performance degradation in BD-Rate. The parallel pipeline architecture supports real-time encoding of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3840\times 2160$</tex> @60fps.

articleTitle: Continuous Monitoring for Diagnosis: A Wearable for Covid-19 Detection in Symptomatic Patients
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We develop an approach for systematically designing continuous monitoring solutions for early symptom diagnosis. Effective early diagnosis requires collecting and correlating symptoms derived from a number of vitals. For designing a continuous monitoring solution, it is crucial to determine the vitals to be monitored for targeted detection, the errors that can be tolerated, various parameters that need to be tuned, etc. Furthermore, this determination must be made before the design of the monitoring solution itself. Our approach shows how to use a variety of machine learning techniques to systematically derive, tune, and optimize the vitals to be monitored before accessing the continuous monitoring data. We show the effectiveness of our approach in the design of a wearable for early detection of COVID-19 infections in symptomatic patients.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Compensation in Wireless Power Transfer Topologies with Application to Contactless Connectors for Consumer Electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Presented in this paper is a technique that addresses misalignment for Non-Metallic Connector (NMC) applications. The technique takes advantage of nonlinear effects of varactor diodes that can be used to function as a nonlinear capacitor. This result can be used to make changes to the compensation capacitance value when there are changes in mutual inductance resulting from misalignment between transmitting (Tx) and receiving (Rx) coils without the need for complex active control feedback systems used in conventional WPT systems. This added flexibility gives rise to a consistent power transfer efficiency (PTE) curve over a specified distance and leads to reduced cost in required component count in micro-WPT (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \text{WPT}$</tex>) systems especially in application to NMCs. In addition to being applied to WPT-based smartphone chargers, this technique can be applied to any number of CE NMC applications where misalignment would impact PTE. Within the last few years contactless connectivity within industry has mostly been focused on high-speed signal transfer protocols such as ethernet, USB, UART, etc. but there remain challenges in power transfer due partly to expensive active feedback control systems. This new technique advances that effort, and this paper not only shows how it can work but does so with application to automation connectors that multiple connector companies are currently focused on.

articleTitle: A Study of Recognition Method of Curved Surface Reflector Code by LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, the convenience of road transportation has been remarkably improved by the spread of automobiles. However, there are problems of frequent traffic accidents and traffic congestions, and ITS (Intelligent Transport Systems) has been actively researched to solve these problems. ITS has several elements such as inter-vehicle communication, roadside-to-vehicle communication, and autonomous sensing with cameras and ladars. We propose a new autonomous sensing that uses infrared laser radar to detect reflector code on the roadside strip and acquire information. Infrared laser radar mounted on a vehicle scans the reflector code of the roadside strip while the vehicle is in motion. However, conventional methods have problems such as low speeds at which the vehicle can be scanned and decreased recognition accuracy as the vehicle speed increases. To solve these problems, this paper proposes to use LiDAR as a scanning device to improve vehicle speed and recognition accuracy. The intensity of the 3D point cloud data obtained by LiDAR can be used to discriminate the kind of reflectors. In the performance evaluation, we have confirmed that scanning at 30 km/h is possible. In the performance evaluation of recognition accuracy, we have confirmed that it can recognize the reflector code completely.

articleTitle: iPhone 240fps Video Dataset for Various Model Training Tasks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: High frame rate videos are recently used for training a variety of image processing tasks such as image/video deblurring and frame interpolation. Yet, the number of publicly available datasets with high frame rate videos are still limited. In this paper, we propose the iPhone 240fps dataset, a dataset which consists of real world 240fps videos. We conduct experiments with deblurring and frame interpolation models to show the effectiveness of this dataset. We also use this dataset to conduct experiments with a state-of-the-art video super-resolution model. We take advantage of the flexibility to change the frame rate of the dataset and test which fps is best suited for training the model. We believe this dataset can make contributions to future works in image and video processing. articleTitle: An Improved Flash-Based Swap System for Performance and Flash Endurance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recently, CE devices are increasingly supporting various features that meet user requirements, and accordingly, the demand for the amount of memory required continues to increase. Compression swap technology, which stores compressed data in memory, is widely used as a solution to secure free memory, but fundamentally, compressed data occupies the memory. On the other hand, the traditional disk swap method using disk as a swap device has the advantage of not requiring memory occupancy, but in an embedded environment, it has been difficult to be widely used due to the overall system performance degradation due to disk I/O operation and the lifespan limit of flash as a disk device. In this work, we present a method to minimize the overhead caused by I/O by screening swap data to be stored in flash as a way to solve the performance and life limitations that have hindered the use of flash swap. At the same time, it shows how to asynchronously writeback the swap data and how to utilize the enhanced mode of flash to overcome the flash lifespan limit. As a result of the evaluation, our scheme shows performance degradation of less than 5 % on average in the DTV user scenario compared to the existing compression swap technology in a DTV environment using total 1.5GB memory, while free memory improves by more than 130MB in idle time.

articleTitle: Two-Step Self-Supervised Pretraining Approach for Machinist Hand Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: We propose a two-step self-supervised pretraining approach for hand gesture recognition on an assembly line. Obtaining adequate company-specific data from an assembly line for machine learning is difficult because of the frequent need for confidentiality and the cost of annotation. To overcome this quantitative limitation, we propose an approach that performs self-supervised pretraining in two steps using data that are similar to the target data and relatively easier to obtain. In the experiment, the machinist dataset, which is a subset of the Yale Human Grasping dataset, was used as hand gesture data from an assembly line. By comparing different pretraining method and dataset, two-step self-supervised pretraining yielded highest accuracy, showing the improvement obtained by our method. The result indicates that our method has the potential to improve specific hand gesture recognition without expensive data preparation.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Sensor Module for Antarctica Exploration Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In cryogenic regions, robots need various sensors to autonomously drive and perform their missions. These sensors should not only provide data for recognizing the environment, avoiding obstacles, and detecting their location, but should also be able to operate in a cryogenic environment. In this paper, we propose a multimodal sensor module that can acquire RGB, depth, and thermal images for use in a cryogenic environment (e.g. the Antarctic). The proposed module can explore crevasses while autonomously driving in Antarctica together with 3D Lidar and GPS sensors.

articleTitle: Spectral Estimation from Actual Color Images based on Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Spectral information can be recovered from color images to preserve high spectral and spatial resolutions simultaneously. Synthetic color images are generally used in the present methods. However, the synthetic color images might not conform to the data distribution of actual color images. In this study, a real dataset is constructed with actual color images acquired with color cameras. Besides, a deep neural network is designed using residual neural network, to retrieve the spectral reflectances from the RGB values of the color images. The proposed network is verified via a 5-fold cross validation, and the findings indicate that the proposed network can obtain higher accuracy than the two existing spectral estimation algorithms with respect to the constructed dataset.

articleTitle: A Time-Based Digital Interface for RF and Baseband IC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a digital interface between RF and baseband IC in 5G system. The interface is based on a source synchronous clocking as in DDR (Double Data Rate). This interface provides a constant group delay and a simplified retransmission scheme. There are two different data types: one is a lossy data; the other is a reliable data. To handle both types, we provides two types of data path: Default path and Safe path. The data lane is a single ended; the clock signal is differential signal. The max data rate per lane is 6.6Gbps. The area of 8 lanes for downlink and 4 lanes for uplink is about 1.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 4 nm process. The power efficiency is 6.8pJ/bit.

articleTitle: Short-Time Fatigue Estimation System Utilizing Web camera and Re-Learning Function
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In recent years, it becomes a social problem that the number of deaths due to overwork is increasing. The cause of the problem is the accumulation of daily mental and physical fatigue, and the trend is expected to continue. On the other hand, in the existing studies, a fatigue measurement system using a general-purpose RGB camera has been proposed. However, in the existing system, the camera should take about one minute to capture the user's face and the recorded video is analyzed to identify the degree of fatigue, which is a heavy burden on the user. Therefore, in our previous study, we propose a new system that a short-time video of a specific user's face is created using a web camera, and the video is analyzed using the image analysis and machine learning technologies to estimate the degree of fatigue in three levels. However, to build a machine learning model, it is necessary to generate training data by capturing the user's face for a long period of time in advance. In addition, the machine learning model constructed for a specific user cannot estimate the fatigue level of other users with high accuracy. Therefore, in this study, we propose an extension function to expand advantages of the system to many users. Specifically, to estimate the degree of fatigue for many users with high accuracy and low load for the user, we propose a re-learning method that can modify the machine learning model constructed for the specific user to new models that can be used for other users.

articleTitle: A Study of Promoting Relaxation System Using Extra-Conscious Sounds Containing Alpha Ultra-Low Frequency Monaural Beats
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This study proposes a relaxation system using alpha-band monaural beats to promote relaxation in people. To avoid affecting human activity, the frequency of the stimulus sound used to generate the target beat is outside the frequency range of human auditory perception. To examine the performance of the proposed method, a subjective test and a MindWave single-electrode electroencephalogram (EEG) tester were used to check meditation values. A paired-samples <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> test was used to verify the relaxation values for both methods. As a result of the experiment, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> value of the EEG meditation value of the 6th minute was 0.04, and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> value of the subjective scale was 0.0075. The experimental results show that the proposed method can reveal a certain relaxation effect. Therefore, the proposed relaxing system can actually promote people's relaxation.

articleTitle: Top-K Confidence Map Aggregation for Robust Semantic Segmentation Against Unexpected Degradation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have become the mainstream for computer vision tasks like semantic segmentation. The CNNs have substantially improved the performance of semantic segmentation. The implicit assumption for those CNN approaches is that the input image is clean without any image degradation. In an actual situation, however, the input image contains many unexpected image degradations such as noise, blur, or compression distortion. The performance of the conventional CNN approach is severely degraded by those unexpected image degradations. This paper presents a simple framework that makes the semantic segmentation algorithms robust against image degradation without re-training the original semantic segmentation CNN. Our key observation is that the down-sampled image is less sensitive to various types of degradation than the original-sized image. Therefore, we adopt a multi-scale test time augmentation (TTA). In the multi-scale TTA, the input image is firstly down-sampled with multiple scales. Then, inferred confidence maps are aggregated to obtain the final inference result. We also propose a top-K confidence map aggregation to further performance improvement. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework is more robust than existing methods for images with degradations and a real compressed video with H.264.

articleTitle: Bicycle Gear Shifting Prediction Using Environmental Information and Physiological Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This paper presents the bicycle gear shifting prediction techniques using environmental information and physiological data. With the development of an intelligent bike platform, actual riding data are collected for model training. Different from previous research on automatic transmission for vehicles, bicycle gear shifting prediction needs to consider also human factors as the power source, and poses a more challenging problem. In this work, we present several machine learning methods for the gear prediction and analysis. To deal with the theoretically correct but unpleasant high-frequency gear switches for the ride, a two-stage training framework incorporated with the past gear information is proposed. The evaluation results demonstrated that XGBoost and CATBoost are able to provide accurate gear shift prediction. It also shows the feasibility of the proposed techniques applicable to the real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Power-saving Sensor Network System for Detection of Harmful Animals by Step-by-step Sensor Linkage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In Japan, technology to remotely detect the presence of animals is attracting attention in order to decrease damage to crops by animals. In our previous research, we have developed a power-saving wildlife observation system that detects the animals by various sensors equipped with edge devices. This system improves the power efficiency of sensor nodes by linking sensors with different power consumption and sensing technologies. However, the problem with this method is that the accuracy of the estimation decreases significantly as the distance between the thermal camera and the target increases. Therefore, in this study, we conduct research and development of wild animals detection system that estimates the type, number, and posture of wild animals by processing and analyzing point clouds measured using 3D LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging), which can accurately measure the distance to an object and its shape. In addition, the proposed system reduces the power consumption of sensor nodes, assuming installation in mountainous areas where there is no commercial power. To reduce power consumption at sensor nodes, the system activates the 3D LiDAR only when a low-power radio beacon device detects the target.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of A New Multiplexer Design for Adaptive Logic
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Field Programmable Gate Arrays are essential components in applications, which require a certain degree of recon-figurability. This feature is achieved by a sea of configurable logic blocks, which realize the desired boolean functions. These blocks require interconnect lanes to realize more complex functions and to exchange data. In consequence, interconnect logic consumes a comparably large amount of each FPGA type, where multiplexers are an integral part. These components can be realized in different ways with different advantages and drawbacks. In this paper, selected multiplexer designs are compared to a versatile, newly developed, data retaining and power saving multiplexer design.

articleTitle: Phase-Change Memory using Cu2GeTe3 and Multiple Writing Technique for Neuromorphic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: A phase-change memory (PCM) using Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>GeTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (CGT) and multiple writing technique have been developed for neuromorphic systems. First, the PCM using CGT is fabricated. Next, the single writing technique as a conventional technique is tried, but reproducible operation is required. Therefore, the multiple writing technique for reliable operation is proposed, and it is confirmed that the multiple RESET pulses contribute to it. Finally, the associative memory function by the neuromorphic system is validated.

articleTitle: Edge-Assisted Object Detection Using Eye Tracking Function of Mixed Reality Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Although object detection methods have significant potential to extend the boundaries of mixed reality (MR), they are often difficult to execute on current MR devices that have limited computing resources. In this paper, we propose an edge-assisted object detection method that uses the eye-tracking function of MR devices to determine whether an object detection task should be offloaded to an edge server for processing and thus reduce the MR device processing load. We implement and evaluate the proposed method using a Microsoft HoloLens 2 to confirm its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Head Movement Modeling for Immersive Visualization in VR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Virtual Reality, and Extended Reality in general, connect the physical body with the virtual world. Movement of our body translates to interactions with this virtual world. Only by moving our head will we see a different perspective. By doing so, the physical restrictions of our body's movement restrict our capabilities virtually. By modelling the capabilities of human movement, render engines can get useful information to pre-cache visual texture information or immersive light information. Such pre-caching becomes vital due to ever increasing realism in virtual environments. This work is the first work to predict the volume in which the head will be positioned in the future based on a data-driven binned-ellipsoid technique. The proposed technique can reduce a 1m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> volume to a size of 10cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with negligible accuracy loss. This volume then provides the render engine with the necessary information to pre-cache visual data.

articleTitle: Daily Precipitation Prediction Based on Multimodal Representation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Short-term weather forecasting is of great significance to people's lives, especially in terms of transportation. Since daily precipitation can be regarded as a nonlinear and non-stationary time series, it is difficult to predict it. Based on the contrastive learning method, A multimodal representation method for forecasting daily precipitation is proposed. Specifically, an encoder is used to convert the original weather data into feature representation, then it is optimized through contrastive learning, and the optimized features are used for prediction.

articleTitle: See-Through-Vehicle for Overtaking Activity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: The level of the immersive experience of users in Augmented Reality (AR) systems is important to blend digital augmented objects with the real-world environment. In this paper, we developed a see-through vehicle system to overcome the issues of safe overtaking and solve the problem of occlusion by large vehicles. For this, we used cameras in two cars and a windshield display in the rear car for displaying the see-through effect. The car segmentation was performed on the server inside the rear car and the front car video was displayed on the segmented part of the vehicle. We utilize atrous-based convolution on segmented images. This see-through system will guide the driver about the hidden traffic scenario occluded by the front vehicle. For these experiments, we have attained a performance accuracy of 97.1%.

articleTitle: Circulation of Transformed Image Derivatives with Parameterized Aliasing in the Off-Chain Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: In major NFT marketplaces, digital image contents such as illustrations and photographs generally reside off-chain due to cost, performance, and privacy concerns. InterPlanetary File System (IPFS), a decentralized storage system, is widely used to store and distribute off-chain data of NFT artworks. Applications of digital images generally require displaying, printing, and redistributing them in a variety of sizes, colors, and formats. Unfortunately, the content addressing in IPFS impedes reusing transformation results derived from an original image since totally different IDs from the original must be given for them. They can never comprehend any relation and transition between the original and derivatives. We introduce on-demand image transform functionality and cooperated ID aliasing capability into IPFS for identifying images generated through a transform with a combination of an original's ID and parameters of the applied transform. Our implementation allows retrieving results of newly demanded transforms by inquiring about corresponding IDs for the aliases to others. A preliminary experimental result demonstrates that the proposed ID aliasing can mitigate the processing overhead by promoting reclaiming of transformed images.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Time Sample Replacement Scheme in OFDM System Using NU-QAM Under Impulsive Noise Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: Recently, OFDM modulation schemes have been used in various applications. The influence of impulsive noise in the channel is a problem in OFDM. Impulsive noise is often found in man-made noise and is characterized by short time widths and very high amplitudes. Sources of the noise include discharge noise from power lines and switching noise from electronic equipment. Since Impulsive noise has a wide frequency range, it affects all OFDM carrier waves. Therefore, the influence of impulsive noise in the receiver must be reduced. Time Sample Replacement scheme has been proposed as a method for reduction of the influence of impulsive noise. The effectiveness of Time Sample Replacement scheme in OFDM systems employing Non Uniform QAM (NU-QAM), which has been proposed as a new modulation scheme for the next generation, is evaluated.
